note: Which lesson each hexagram with a character drawing gets: its current lesson (series/lessons.json) or the character (series/characters.json). 42 is decided by the author: the character. Scored by scripts/workflows/lesson-treatment.js.

current.text:
Lake gone dry?
Hold to your aim.
current.why: The Image: the lake without water is oppression, and the realized person stakes their life on following their purpose. Both readers got the empty lake but no lesson.

character.story: A tree stands; walls rise round it; it is pressed flat inside them.
character.sentence:
Pressed in,
keep growing

decision.text:
Pressed in,
keep growing
decision.why: The walls pressing the tree flat show 困 (oppression) directly; the lake image needs explaining.

current.text:
Plan three days,
check three days.
current.why: The Judgment puts three days before a new start and three days after it, so a repair gets time on both sides.

character.story: Worms breed in a shut bowl, swarm up and pour out.
character.sentence:
What you leave
shut goes bad

decision.text:
What you leave
shut goes bad
decision.why: Worms swarming out of a shut bowl is the character and the hexagram (decay you must fix) at once.

current.text:
The well is clean.
No one drinks.
current.why: Line 3, the only sad line in the book: the well is cleaned and no one drinks, 'my heart's sorrow'.

character.story: Four beams rise as the well's frame; the water in the middle ripples on every beat.
character.sentence:
The town changes;
the well stays

decision.text:
The well is clean.
No one drinks.
decision.why: The well clip is the weakest: four beams and a ripple. "The well is clean. No one drinks." is a clear, odd image.

current.text:
Without a guide,
let the deer go.
current.why: Line 3: chasing deer into the forest without a forester goes wrong, so let it go.

character.story: A sprout stands buried to its tip; it pushes up through the ground in three strains, then lies down as the character.
character.sentence:
Starts are
always hard.

decision.text:
Starts are
always hard.
decision.why: The sprout straining up through the ground is 屯 (difficult beginnings) exactly.

current.text:
No game in this
field. Move.
current.why: Persistence in the wrong place is wasted: a field with no game.

character.story: Two lines rise; between them a moon goes from new to full and back, then sets into them; a heart is drawn beside it.
character.sentence:
Change shape,
keep your course

decision.text:
Change shape,
keep your course
decision.why: The moon changing shape between two steady lines shows constancy through change; the current line needs context.

current.text:
A prince acted mad
to stay alive.
current.why: Line 5: Prince Ji hid his sanity at the tyrant's court, the book's own example of hiding your light to survive.

character.story: A window rises; beside it a full moon shines, then wanes to a thin crescent that stays lit, and sets into the moon's strokes.
character.sentence:
Keep your light
low and on

decision.text:
Keep your light
low and on
decision.why: Keeping a light low but on is the hexagram (light hidden in dark times); the prince story needs history. The waning moon is our own story of 明, not its etymology.

current.text:
The legs break.
Duke wears dinner.
current.why: The caldron's legs break, the duke's meal spills over him: what happens when the setup isn't right.

character.story: The legs rise; a fire is lit among them; the bowl, drawn high above, drops onto them.
character.sentence:
A steady base
lets things cook

decision.text:
A steady base
lets things cook
decision.why: The cauldron set on its legs over a fire shows 鼎 plainly; the duke joke is funny but is about one line.

current.text:
Riding with a load
invites thieves.
current.why: Line 3: carrying the old burden into freedom makes you a target.

character.story: The ox and its horn are drawn; a knife rises beside them; the horn lifts free and hovers.
character.sentence:
Cut it loose
and move on

decision.text:
Cut it loose
and move on
decision.why: The horn cut free is 解 (release) in the character itself.

current.text:
Uninvited guests?
Receive them well.
current.why: Line 6: three uninvited guests arrive; treat them with respect and it ends well.

character.story: A figure stands; a cloud forms above and rain falls on it; it waits; the rain stops, the cloud comes down and the figure lies down under it.
character.sentence:
Wait in the rain;
it will pass.

decision.text:
Wait in the rain;
it will pass.
decision.why: Waiting out the rain is 需 (waiting); the guests line is one line flavour. The example short showed it works.

current.text:
Too comfortable?
Worry a little.
current.why: Line 3: a comfortable approach supports nothing, but once you worry about it there is no fault.

character.story: A figure with a big eye stands, leans down, and three small squares light up under it one by one; then it lies down as the character.
character.sentence:
Lean down to
see what is small

decision.text:
Lean down to
see what is small
decision.why: The big eye leaning down to look at small things is 臨 (overseeing, drawing near).

current.text:
Stillness starts
in the back.
current.why: The Judgment opens with 'Stilling the back', the part you can't see, not the face or the mind. A specific, surprising detail.

character.story: A figure with a big eye stands, turns round to look back, holds still, turns forward again and lies down as the character.
character.sentence:
Stop, and look
at where you are

decision.text:
Stop, and look
at where you are
decision.why: The figure turning round to look and holding still teaches stopping; "Stillness starts in the back" is harder to picture.

current.text:
The bed breaks at
the legs first.
current.why: Collapse starts at the base, the part nobody looks at.

character.story: A knife stands beside a block; pieces fall off the block one by one until only its base stands; then both lie down as the character.
character.sentence:
Stripped back
to the base

decision.text:
Stripped back
to the base
decision.why: Pieces falling off the block until only the base stands is 剝 (stripping away).

current.text:
The wanderer burns
his own inn.
current.why: A guest who wrecks the shelter he was given loses his helper too.

character.story: People under a flag are drawn standing far off; they walk toward you in four hops, then lie down as the character.
character.sentence:
Travel light;
keep moving

decision.text:
Travel light;
keep moving
decision.why: People walking toward you with a flag is 旅 (travelling); the burnt inn is one line.

current.text:
Painters toast,
then talk shop.
current.why: Krøyer's artists at their party: the Image joins friends for discussion and practice, not only celebration.

character.story: A figure's mouth rises open; the two lines above it lift out of it and float, bobbing, like laughter.
character.sentence:
Joy is better
shared out loud

decision.text:
Joy is better
shared out loud
decision.why: The lines lifting out of an open mouth like laughter is 兌 (joy); the painting lesson is about one painting.

current.text:
Friends at lunch,
holding together.
current.why: Accepted: Renoir's crowded table shows holding together at a glance.

character.story: One figure stands; a second stands behind it, then walks up in three hops to stand close beside it; they lie down together as the character.
character.sentence:
Choose who you
stand beside

decision.text:
Choose who you
stand beside
decision.why: A second figure walking up to stand beside the first is 比 (holding together).

current.text:
Parted, they weep.
Met, they laugh.
current.why: Line 5: fellowship first weeps and wails, then laughs when the armies manage to meet. Both readers got sad-then-happy but not that the tears come from being apart and the laughter from meeting.

character.story: A frame rises; inside it a board and a mouth are drawn, and all of it inside lifts at once, together, and hovers.
character.sentence:
Lift it
together

decision.text:
Parted, they weep.
Met, they laugh.
decision.why: The 同 clip (a frame, the inside lifting) reads weakly as "together"; the line "Parted, they weep. Met, they laugh." is strong.

current.text:
Fine silk turns
to rags.
current.why: After completion, decay is slow and quiet, so the line says to stay watchful all day.

character.story: A figure stands; a bowl rises beside it; the meal done, the figure turns its back on the bowl, holds, turns again and lies down as the character.
character.sentence:
When it is done,
stay awake

decision.text:
When it is done,
stay awake
decision.why: Turning away from the finished meal and staying awake is 既濟 (after completion, stay careful).

current.text:
Midwinter: rest.
The light returns.
current.why: The Image: thunder within the earth is return, so the kings closed the passes at the solstice and no one travelled. Both readers asked why they stayed home: the stillness lets what is coming back return.

character.story: A passage rises; a foot stands out in front of it, then walks back toward it in four hops; the road it walks is drawn after it.
character.sentence:
The way out is
the way back

decision.text:
The way out is
the way back
decision.why: The foot walking back into the passage is 復 (return).

current.text:
Stood on a tiger's
tail. Not bitten.
current.why: The Judgment: treading on the tiger's tail, it does not bite the person. Both readers read the old text as a harmless tail; it has to say someone stands on the tail and the tiger still does not bite.

character.story: A figure with a big eye stands; its foot comes down in front of it one stroke at a time, a beat apart, each placed with care; then it lies down as the character.
character.sentence:
Watch where
you step

decision.text:
Stood on a tiger's
tail. Not bitten.
decision.why: The foot coming down is subtle in the clip; the tiger tail judgment is the best known image of 履.

current.text:
Stop staring at
someone's plate.
current.why: Line 1 sets down its own spirit tortoise to gape at someone else's meal: envy traded for self-sufficiency.

character.story: A head is drawn; beside it an open jaw rises; what is inside the jaw rises and spills out over its rim.
character.sentence:
Mind what goes in
and what comes out

decision.text:
Mind what goes in
and what comes out
decision.why: The open jaw with things spilling out teaches minding what goes in and comes out, which is 頤 (nourishment).
